cohort.label: Jul–Aug 2016 Board of Education (Lee Chair)
cohort.transition_reason: Swearing-in of March 15, 2016 election winners: Steve Unruhe (At-Large, succeeding retiring Leigh Bordley), Xavier Cason (Consolidated District B, succeeding outgoing Chair Heidi Carter who ran for Durham Board of County Commissioners), and unopposed incumbent Minnie Forte-Brown (Consolidated District A). Mike Lee elected Chair; Natalie Beyer elected Vice Chair.

cohesion.label: High Consensus
cohesion.note: Only 0 split vote(s) recorded across 1 meetings — this board-term has largely voted unanimously.

overall_blocs.summary: No recorded split votes in this scope yet (board voted unanimously on tracked motions).

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session August 11, 2016
conflicts.issue: Policy 2302 on Remote Participation in Board Meetings
conflicts.summary: Board members disagreed over whether to adopt formal remote-participation rules in Policy 2302 after public commenters attacked the proposal as excusing Sendolo Diaminah's absences.
conflicts.side_a_position: Avoid adopting Policy 2302 or keep remote participation strictly ad hoc/case-by-case.
side_a_arguments: Steve Unruhe warned that adopting a formal policy gives the public the impression the board encourages remote attendance.
Xavier Cason preferred leaving the seven-member board's long-standing case-by-case practice untouched unless legally required to change.
Natalie Beyer emphasized the importance of in-person attendance and urged waiting for Minnie Forte-Brown and Sendolo Diaminah before any decision.
conflicts.side_b_position: Establish clear written policy parameters allowing remote call-in for work travel or medical recovery.
side_b_arguments: Dr. Mike Lee argued that clear written guidelines provide fair flexibility for working board members who travel or face medical recovery without replacing ad hoc rules with guesswork.
Matt Sears noted the board had previously failed to explain members' out-of-town call-in reasons clearly to constituents while expressing openness to keeping an informal trust-based approach.
conflicts.resolution: Postponed without a formal vote to a future work session so absent members Minnie Forte-Brown and Sendolo Diaminah could participate.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Operational Services and Policy Work Session August 11, 2016
meetings.executive_summary: At the August 11, 2016 Operational Services and Policy Work Session—presided over by committee chair Xavier Cason with Minnie Forte-Brown and Sendolo Diaminah absent—the five attending board members unanimously approved the agenda, June 16 minutes, FY 2015–16 Budget Amendment #3 ($420,713,644 final appropriation), purchasing three replacement activity buses, placing a minority-owned contract transportation renewal on the August 25 action agenda, and the Waste Industries waste and recycling contract amended to align with House Bill 2 livable-wage provisions. Members also reviewed a 6.1% reduction in district insurance premiums and endorsed transitioning from the 20-plus-member Budget Advisory Committee to a 12-member Zero-Based Budgeting Committee facilitated by UNC's Dr. Eric Houck. On Policy 2302 (Remote Participation in Board Meetings), public commenters condemned the draft as a shield for absent board member Sendolo Diaminah, while Xavier Cason, Steve Unruhe, and Natalie Beyer favored relying on existing ad hoc/case-by-case practices over Chair Dr. Mike Lee's preference for written flexibility guidelines; the board deferred the item to a future work session without a vote. The board also voted 5-0 to forward work session start times and off-site school pilots to the August full board action agenda before entering closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding committee chair Xavier Cason opened the work session with a moment of silence and announced positive news that Durham student Wilden Acosta might soon return to DPS to complete his graduation. On a motion by Dr. Mike Lee seconded by Natalie Beyer, the board approved the agenda 5-0 (with Minnie Forte-Brown and Sendolo Diaminah absent).

agenda_items.title: Approval of June 16, 2016 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Natalie Beyer moved and Xavier Cason seconded approval of the June 16, 2016 Operational Services and Policy Work Session minutes. The motion passed unanimously, 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers included Lucia Gutierrez (accompanied by Nicole), Dr. Anita Keith-Foust (facility inequities), Jackie Wagstaff (requesting a nonverbal-conduct policy and opposing the $90 million bond, Duke Homestead land banking, and remote meeting participation), Riverside teacher Brian Christopher (Hope Street Group teacher voice survey), and Allen Lang (supporting school-based meetings while urging that remote participation Policy 2302 be scrapped).

agenda_items.title: FY 2015–16 Budget Amendment #3
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public skepticism from Dr. Anita Keith-Foust over historical budget amendments and fund balances, CFO Aaron Beaulieu presented year-end Budget Amendment #3, bringing final FY 2015–16 appropriations to $420,713,644 (a $1,508,913 increase over Amendment #2, with roughly $385 million spent and state/federal grant carryovers ahead of the December CAFR audit). Steve Unruhe moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval of Budget Amendment #3, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Budget Advisory Committee Transition to Zero-Based Budgeting Committee
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Aaron Beaulieu and Matt Sears proposed suspending the 20-plus-member Budget Advisory Committee for one year in favor of a 12-member Zero-Based Budgeting Committee (one appointee per board member, one board member, one county commissioner, one DAE rep, one administrator, and one teacher) meeting monthly through May 2017 under outside facilitator Dr. Eric Houck of UNC. Board members supported the restructuring by consensus, urged demographic and school-level diversity, requested clarity on facilitator/teacher compensation and alternates, and set an August 21 target for board appointments.

agenda_items.title: Purchase of Three Replacement Activity Buses
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff requested immediate approval to purchase three activity buses waiting at the state-contract vendor to replace aging units among DPS's 40-bus fleet (13 buses aged 19+ years, including six 25-year-old buses). After Chair Lee asked about multi-year vendor financing options—which staff agreed to evaluate for next year—Matt Sears moved and Steve Unruhe seconded approval of the three-bus purchase, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Annual Insurance Program Renewal Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mr. Denton reported under Policy 7410 that the district's broker negotiated a 6.1% overall reduction in annual insurance premiums effective July 1 without reducing coverage levels, exceeding the 5% target. Board members thanked staff for absorbing risk-management duties after position eliminations.

agenda_items.title: Contract Transportation Renewal Referral
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a one-year contract (renewable for four years) with two incumbent Durham minority-owned contractors transporting outlier students outside regular bus routes, raising the per-child per-trip rate from $16.47 (unchanged for five years) to $17.50 with up to a 1% annual administrative fuel-adjustment option. Because the full contract text was omitted from the packet, Natalie Beyer moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded placing the item on the August 25 regular meeting action agenda, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Waste and Recycling Contract (Waste Industries)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a competitive five-year waste and recycling contract (one year plus four renewals) with incumbent Waste Industries totaling roughly $330,000 plus a $20,000 allowance (about $19,000 higher), explaining the City of Durham lacked fleet capacity to bid. Board attorney Ken Soo modified page five's House Bill 2-compliant wording from "living wage policy" to "livable wage provision of this agreement," and Dr. Mike Lee moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval with that modification, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Exit Interviews (K12 Insight) and Formative 360 Principal Feedback (Hanover Research)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matt Sears and staff outlined plans to improve teacher-retention data using anonymous third-party exit surveys via K12 Insight starting after January and a formative (non-evaluative) 360-degree leadership feedback process via Hanover Research phased from principals to central office and assistant principals. Board members welcomed the initiatives and asked that the Principal and Teacher Advisory Groups help shape survey questions.

agenda_items.title: Policy 2302: Remote Participation in Board Meetings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public opposition from Jackie Wagstaff and Allen Lang targeting Sendolo Diaminah's absences, Dr. Pittman outlined NCSBA's optional Policy 2302 parameters while Natalie Beyer, Steve Unruhe, and Xavier Cason objected that adopting a formal policy sent the wrong message or preferred keeping case-by-case ad hoc practice. Dr. Mike Lee argued for clear written flexibility for unavoidable work travel or surgical recovery, and after Attorney Ken Soo noted school boards face no statutory remote-quorum ban (unlike county commissioners), members agreed without a vote to postpone further discussion to a work session when Minnie Forte-Brown and Diaminah could attend.

agenda_items.title: Board Work Session Times and Off-Site Locations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members discussed holding two pilot work sessions in high schools (such as School for Creative Studies or northern and southern high schools), technical livestreaming requirements, and shifting work session start times from 4:00 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. to match 4:00 p.m. high school dismissal times. Dr. Mike Lee moved and Natalie Beyer seconded placing the item on the August full board action agenda, passing 5-0.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members requested a definitive written accounting of the 2007 bond High School A / fund-balance history and updates on a Southern High bus parking-lot surface dispute with an adjacent owner before voting 5-0 to enter closed session for the reasons listed on the agenda.

votes.notes: Minnie Forte-Brown (absent for health reasons per 01:36:39) and Sendolo Diaminah (absent per 01:40:57) were not present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the work session agenda as presented.

votes.item_title: Approve June 16, 2016 Operational Services and Policy Work Session Minutes
votes.notes: Five members present; Minnie Forte-Brown and Sendolo Diaminah absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved June 16, 2016 work session minutes as presented.

votes.notes: Mover transcribed as 'Mr. Andrews' (Steve Unruhe); five members present.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved year-end Budget Amendment #3 increasing total FY 2015–16 appropriations by $1,508,913 to $420,713,644.

votes.item_title: Approve Purchase of Three Replacement Activity Buses
votes.discussion_detail: Approved immediate purchase of three state-contract activity buses to replace aging units while asking staff to review multi-year financing options for future years.

votes.item_title: Place Contract Transportation Renewal on August 25 Action Agenda
votes.discussion_detail: Referred the one-year (four-year renewable) outlier transportation contract with two Durham minority-owned firms to the August 25 regular meeting so the full contract document could be attached.

votes.item_title: Approve Waste and Recycling Contract with Waste Industries (As Amended)
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the ~$330,000 (+$20,000 allowance) Waste Industries waste and recycling contract incorporating attorney Ken Soo's HB2-compliant 'livable wage provision of this agreement' wording on page five.

votes.item_title: Place Work Session Times and Locations on August Regular Meeting Action Agenda
votes.discussion_detail: Forwarded proposals for shifting work sessions to 4:30 p.m. and piloting school-site meetings to the August 25 full board action agenda.
Entered closed session for the statutory reasons stated on the agenda.
